script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

A modern, open-concept kitchen. Sunlight streams in through large windows. JOHN (early 40s, disheveled) stands at the sink, washing dishes. He's lost in thought.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
John, a failed restaurateur, wonders how he'll pay his debts and win back his estranged family.

Suddenly, the doorbell rings. John looks surprised.

JOHN
(calling out)
Coming!

INT. ENTRANCEWAY - CONTINUOUS

John opens the door to reveal ANNA (late 30s, dressed elegantly). She carries a small basket.

ANNA
Good morning, John. I brought you some bread.

John looks at her, confused.

JOHN
Anna? I haven't seen you in years.

ANNA
Yes, it's been a while. I wanted to see how you're doing.

John invites her in, unsure of her intentions.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

Anna sits on the couch, chatting amiably while John makes coffee.

ANNA
I heard about your restaurant closing. I'm so sorry, John.

JOHN
(sighs)
It's been a disaster. But I'm trying to turn things around.

ANNA
(smiling)
That's the spirit. I have an idea that might help.

INT. KITCHEN - LATER

Anna demonstrates a unique pasta dish she's invented. John watches in awe as she cooks.

ANNA
I think this could be the dish that saves your restaurant, John.

JOHN
(excited)
Really? You think so?

INT. RESTAURANT - DAY

John prepares the new pasta dish for his customers. The dining room is nearly empty.

WAITER
(nervously)
Boss, there's a couple who wants to try the new dish.

JOHN
(nervously)
Okay, send them over.

INT. DINING ROOM - LATER

The couple, MARK (early 40s) and LIZ (late 30s), enjoy the pasta and compliment John on his culinary skills.

MARK
This is fantastic, John. We'll definitely be back.

LIZ
Absolutely. It's a shame more people don't know about this place.

JOHN
(smiling)
Maybe with your help, we can change that.

INT. JOHN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

John sits at his kitchen table, contemplating a newspaper article about his restaurant's success. Anna enters, a smile on her face.

ANNA
I'm glad to see things are looking up for you, John.

JOHN
(gratefully)
I couldn't have done it without you, Anna.

ANNA
(teasingly)
I'll take that as a compliment.

JOHN
(laughs)
It is. And I mean it sincerely.

Anna leans in for a hug.

ANNA
I'm glad we've reconnected, John. It feels like a second chance for both of us.

FADE OUT.

THE END
